response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord r ON a.translink = r.transreg JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, 1.0 * cnt / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), av AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT s.tradekind, s.cnt AS behaviour_count, s.share, s.share - av.avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM s CROSS JOIN av WHERE av.avg_share IS NOT NULL AND s.share > av.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: The amount of behaviour analysis for a trader type is the number of advancedbehavior rows that join through transactionrecord to trader. Inner joins drop non-matching rows.
A NULL tradekind forms its own group, because GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group. It is counted in the total and in the average of shares.
Shares are computed with 1.0 multiplication to avoid integer division and are not rounded. The average is the plain mean of the per-type shares, which equals 1 divided by the number of types.
